question: Which of the following ratios is greatest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Compare fractions by observing the **gap** between numerator and denominator.

For (1) 13/32 and (2) 18/37, the **numerator** is roughly half of the **denominator** (Value ≈ 0.5).

For (3) 23/25 and (4) 25/26, the **gap** is small. 23/25 = 0.92 and 25/26 = 0.96.

Since 0.96 is the highest value, 25 : 26 is the **greatest ratio**.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eae293c230d6f5b7d691e4c54a862c0550951fb1a9d54d344b2e2fbcccda8603.png] 

**Given:** Ratios (1) 13/32, (2) 18/37, (3) 23/25, (4) 25/26

**Method:** Convert each ratio to **decimal form** to compare magnitude.

⇒ Ratio 1 = 13 ÷ 32 ≈ 0.406

⇒ Ratio 2 = 18 ÷ 37 ≈ 0.486

⇒ Ratio 3 = 23 ÷ 25 = (23 × 4) ÷ (25 × 4) = 92 ÷ 100 = 0.92

⇒ Ratio 4 = 25 ÷ 26 ≈ 0.961

⇒ Comparing values: 0.961 > 0.920 > 0.486 > 0.406

**∴ The correct answer is 25 : 26.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Comparison of Fractions with Same Gap

If the difference between numerator and denominator is constant (e.g., 23/25 and 25/27), the fraction with the **larger numbers** is always greater.

Cross-Multiplication Method

To compare a/b and c/d, check the products **a × d** and **b × c**. If ad > bc, then a c/d.

Percentage Conversion

Converting ratios to **percentages** (Ratio × 100) is a quick way to visualize relative sizes in competitive exams.</p
